plumbing.note: The State Building Code Council's page still lists the State Plumbing Code as the 2018 Uniform Plumbing Code (effective May 19, 2020), whose amended section 422.0 sends fixture counts to the building code. No state adoption document for the 2021 edition was found. HRS 107-24(c) makes a model code part of the state codes automatically if the council does not adopt it within two years of publication, and HRS 107-28(b) makes the state codes an interim county code if the county does not amend them within two years; the council's code-cycle chart shows a 2021 UPC state deadline and a later county deadline. That would make the 2021 UPC apply in Honolulu without state or city amendments, including its own fixture table (Table 422.1), which was not read. The text of ROH Chapter 19 itself could not be opened (the online code library blocks automated access).

amendment.text: Honolulu replaces the fixture table with its own and adds three rules. The table's office, restaurant and school rows carry the same ratios as the state's (office 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 after; restaurant 1 per 75; school 1 per 50), and the city's table has no pointer to another code for urinals. New rules: the chapter applies to new construction; urinals may replace no more than 50 percent of the required toilets; and in a new assembly building such as an entertainment center, movie theatre or sports arena, or alterations to existing public assemblies exceeding $500,000, the toilets for women who are not employees must number at least twice those required for men who are not employees. The rest of the section (half men and half women, rounding up, separate rooms and the small-occupancy exceptions, single-user rooms) is not amended by the city.
amendment.quote: (123) Amending Section 2901.1. [...] 2901.1 Scope. Plumbing systems shall comply with the Plumbing Code. (124) [...] 2901.2 Application. The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to new construction. (125) Amending [P] Table 2902.1. [P] Table is amended to read: [P] TABLE 2902.1 MINIMUM NUMBER OF REQUIRED PLUMBING FIXTURES [...] Restaurants, banquet halls, and food courts | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200 [...] 2 Business B | Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, Office Buildings, banks, light industrial, and similar uses | 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 | 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80 [...] 3 Educational E | Educational facilities | 1 per 50 | 1 per 50 [...] a. The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated. The number of occupants shall be determined by this code. [...] d. The occupant load for seasonal outdoor seating and entertainment areas shall be included when determining the minimum number of facilities required. (126) [...] 2902.7 Toilet Facilities in Group A Occupancy. In a building or portion of a building containing a new Group A Occupancy such as an entertainment center, movie theatre, sports area, other similar occupancy, or alterations to existing public assemblies exceeding $500,000, the number of water closets required for females who are not employed in that building shall be at least twice the number available of water closets required for males who are not employed in that building or portion. (127) [...] 2902.8 Urinals. Urinals may be substituted for no more than 50 percent of the required water closets.

fixtures.notes: The table in the ordinance is a scan; the office, restaurant and school rows were read in the OCR text and checked by eye on the page images (ordinance pages 58 and 59). Bars and nightclubs have their own row (1 per 40). Urinals allowed is half the men's toilets rounded down (no more than 50 percent). Section 2902.7 was not applied to the restaurant row: it names entertainment centers, movie theatres and sports arenas 'and other similar occupancy', and whether a restaurant or bar counts is not stated. Sections 2902.1.1 (half and half, rounding), 2902.2 (separate rooms, exceptions for 15 or fewer and for offices of 25 or fewer) and 2902.1.2 are the 2018 model text as read by the state pack on a secondary copy.

permit.exempt_list_quote: 18-3.1 Required. (a) Except as provided in subsection (b), no person shall perform any of the following or cause any of the following to be performed without first obtaining a building permit therefor as prescribed in this chapter: (1) Erect, construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, improve, remove, convert, or demolish any building or structure; [...] (b) Exemptions. Except for construction work to be done within any public utility right-of-way or easement, a permit is not required for the types of work listed below. Exemption from the permit requirements of this code does not grant authorization for any work to be done in violation of the technical codes or any other laws or ordinances of this jurisdiction. [...] (9) Installation of wallpaper or wall covering that is exempted under Chapter 16; (10) Repairs and labor that: (A) Involve the replacement of component parts of existing work with like-for-like materials for the purpose of maintenance; (B) Do not exceed $10,000 in valuation in the aggregate in any 12-month period; and (C) Do not involve any electrical, plumbing, or mechanical installations; (11) Interior remodeling that: (A) Does not affect building square footage or the number of rooms or bathrooms; (B) Does not modify the location of rooms, walls, or windows; and (C) Does not involve any electrical, plumbing, or mechanical installations; including but not limited to painting, installation of floor covering, cabinet and countertop work, and replacement of existing fixtures (such as windows, doors, and appliances); provided that the value of the interior remodeling must be included as part of the value of any new construction for which a permit is required by this code, for the purpose of determining the amount of the fee to be paid for such permit; (12) Work located on federal property, except when permits are specifically requested by the federal agency with administrative authority over the property; (13) Work performed for any government agency, except where permits are specifically requested by the agency; [...] (17) Nonfixed and movable cases, counters, racks, and partitions that do not exceed 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height; [...]
permit.guide_quote: [DPP, Do You Need a Building Permit?] A Word of Caution: This is a general guide. [...] Building Permit Exemptions. Commonly Applicable Items. [...] Repairs using similar or same materials for the purpose of maintenance which are not more than $10,000 in valuation in any 12-month period, and do not affect any electrical or plumbing installations. Painting, cabinet work, floor covering and replacement of windows or doors.
permit.partitions_note: The list names only 'Nonfixed and movable cases, counters, racks, and partitions that do not exceed 5 feet 9 inches' in height. Toilet partitions fixed to the floor, wall or ceiling are not named. Two items could be read to cover a like-for-like replacement (repairs under $10,000 for maintenance; interior remodeling that changes no rooms or walls and replaces existing fixtures), but the list does not say so.

sales_tax.quote: Hawaii does not have a sales tax; instead, we have the GET, which is assessed on all business activities. The tax rate is 0.15% for Insurance Commission, 0.5% for Wholesaling, Manufacturing, Producing, Wholesale Services, and Use Tax on Imports For Resale, and 4% for all others. [...] The following counties have adopted a county surcharge: City and County of Honolulu: 0.5% effective January 1, 2007 to December 31, 2030. [...] a seller may choose to visibly pass on the GE and any applicable county surcharge to its customers, but is not required to do so. The tax is on the business and not on the customer. If the business passes on its GE tax, the maximum pass-on rates, which include the county surcharge if applicable, are as follows: City and County of Honolulu: 4.7120% (effective January 1, 2007 – December 31, 2030)
sales_tax.note: Not a sales tax: a general excise tax on the seller's gross receipts. There is no city or district rate beyond the county surcharge.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions for Honolulu restrooms. Price your layout, pick a material and see the Honolulu building rules and excise tax that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Honolulu hotels, restaurants, office towers and schools.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Honolulu sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and lets urinals replace up to half of the men's toilets. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Honolulu requires a building permit to alter or repair a building and lists the work that needs none. The list covers like-for-like repairs for maintenance worth up to $10,000 in any 12 months, and interior remodeling that leaves rooms, walls and windows where they are, such as painting, floor covering, cabinets, countertops and replacing existing fixtures. Both apply only where no electrical, plumbing or mechanical work is involved. It also covers movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches. It doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall, so ask the Department of Planning and Permitting's Building Division (808-768-8232) whether your replacement needs one. Work done for a government agency needs a permit only if the agency asks for one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under the building rules Honolulu uses, a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. Where toilets are required, the rules call for separate men's and women's rooms and don't cover a shared all-gender room with several stalls, so ask the Department of Planning and Permitting before planning one. Honolulu adds no rule of its own. State law bars places open to the public from discriminating on the basis of gender identity or expression. Buildings open to the public that are designed after July 31, 2027 must include an adult changing station in a public restroom; public schools are exempt.
page.confirm_office: the Honolulu Department of Planning and Permitting
page.stalls_intro: Honolulu's building rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and any fraction rounds up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the required toilets, so the table shows the men's side as stalls.
page.stalls_after: Honolulu applies these counts to new construction. A men's room that needs only one toilet can't swap it for a urinal. An office for up to 25 people, or any space for up to 15, may use one shared restroom. A restaurant's seasonal outdoor seating counts toward the number of people. In a new entertainment center, movie theater, sports arena or similar building, and in alterations costing more than $500,000 to an existing one, there must be at least twice as many toilets for women visitors as for men. Ask the Department of Planning and Permitting how the counts apply to your project.
page.install_rule: Building permit applications in Honolulu list each contractor's Hawaii license number. Hawaii requires a state contractor license unless the whole job, labor and materials together, is $1,500 or less and needs no building permit. The state's institutional and commercial equipment specialty license (C-25) covers stationary metal partitions. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor needs a Hawaii state license for any job over $1,500.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Hawaii requires state-set wages on public construction contracts over $2,000, and the state labor department publishes the rates each February and September. One schedule covers the whole state. For a journeyman carpenter the current rate is $56.75 an hour plus $30.49 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **General excise tax:** Hawaii has no sales tax. Its general excise tax is charged to the business, not the buyer: 4% for the state plus 0.5% for the City and County of Honolulu, 4.5% in all. A business may pass the tax on, and in Honolulu the most it may add to an invoice is 4.712%.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** an installer owes the general excise tax on the full installation price, labor included, and may add it to the invoice.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels and resorts:** phenolic or stainless steel for lobby and restaurant restrooms, HDPE for pool and beach restrooms that stay wet.

notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of fixed toilet partitions in a commercial restroom needs a Honolulu building permit (Department of Planning and Permitting, Building Division, commercial permits 808-768-8232).

Plumbing code: the department's site lists the 2021 Uniform Plumbing Code as Honolulu's interim plumbing code from March 1, 2024, while the State Building Code Council's page still shows the 2018 edition, whose state amendment sends toilet counts to the building code. Ask the department's plumbing reviewers (808-768-8242) whether the toilet counts in Honolulu's own building code table or those in the 2021 plumbing code govern; the page uses the building code table Honolulu adopted in Ordinance 24-15.

Honolulu's toilet-count chapter says it applies to new construction, and its rule doubling women's toilets names entertainment centers, movie theaters and sports arenas: ask the department whether restaurants and bars fall under it and what applies when an existing restroom is altered.

The permit exemptions were read in Ordinance 23-13 (June 2023) and on the department's guide page; the current text of Section 18-3.1 on the online code library, and City Addendum #1 to the building code (effective March 11, 2025), could not be opened by automated access: one browser check.
Which wage classification covers toilet partition installation is not stated in the wage schedule (carpenter was used); the next schedule is due about February 15, 2027.

The page's meta description and lead leave out delivery wording on purpose; the delivery section and the climate paragraph (Honolulu is classed as dry on 16 inches of rain a year) are the generator's standard text and were not adapted for an island, coastal city.
The installation section's contractor rule cites Section 18-4 of the Revised Ordinances on the online code library, which opens in a browser but blocks automated access.
